newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan Archbishop attacks Moi from pulpit.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan Archbishop attacks Moi from pulpit.

text.p: Anglican Archbishop David Gitari on Sunday attacked Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi from the pulpit at Nairobi's All Saints Cathedral at a ceremonial "cleansing" and re-dedication after last week's riots.
Speaking to a packed congregation, who included many opposition figures, Gitari said of Moi: "You have been weighed in the balance and found wanting."

Riot police threw teargas into the cathedral and beat worshippers with batons when people fleeing a confrontation between demonstrators and police sought refuge there last Monday. Senior police officials later publicly apologised for the invasion.
The demonstrations, called to back opposition demands for constitutional reforms ahead of elections due later this year, went ahead in several towns despite a government ban.
Holding aloft one of the teargas canisters hurled into the cathedral on Monday, the Archbishop said that rulers must only be obeyed as long as they do not infringe the rights of their people.

"Blood cannot be shed in a holy place in vain. The government must now put into motion constitutional reforms," the Archbishop said to applause, clearly supporting the opposition stand that without reforms elections should not go ahead.
He added: "There is still hope that the cries of the people will be heard."
Hundreds of Christians surrounded the packed cathedral and joined in the service, relayed by loudspeakers.
They applauded Reverend Timothy Njoya, a Presbyterian, who was hospitalised after being beaten by police in the cathedral on Monday, and appeared wearing a sling and bandages.
A prominent opposition supporter, Njoya called for a boycott of elections unless reforms were implemented.
"Instead of having elections we will open our churches and mosques and teach people what it means to have free and fair elections," he said.
All services in the cathedral were cancelled after Monday's clashes, pending a ceremonial re-dedication.

Before the service Gitari led a procession of Anglican priests around the packed cathedral, waving a ceremonial evergreen branch and sprinkling holy water at the bloodstained spots where one person died and where tear gas cannisters landed.
Firebrand Moslem preacher and one of Moi's most outspoken critics, Sheikh Khalid Balala, joined the service, welcomed by the Archbishop.
Balala, who returned from two years' exile in Germany on Saturday after the Kenya government agreed to admit him, took his place to rapturous applause.

He was on Saturday greeted by hundreds of followers chanting "Moi must go. No reforms, no elections", and said he would organise a 10-million-strong march to force Moi to give in to the growing calls for constitutional changes.
